text: Welcome to the capstone chapter that closes out the Blockchain Engineer path. Everything you've learned so far — Solidity, DApp architecture, DeFi mechanics, testing, and tooling — comes together here, in real projects you build yourself.

You'll build three flagship projects: a full DeFi protocol with pool contracts and a frontend, an NFT marketplace with listings and indexing, and a DAO governance system with voting and a treasury. A final career chapter covers resumes, interviews, and negotiation.

There's no fictional company running through this course. You build each project yourself, under your own name, in your own repository — because the whole point of a capstone is producing something that's genuinely yours to show an employer.

Here's the strategy: two or three deep, complete projects beat a long list of shallow ones. An interviewer skimming your GitHub is looking for real depth — tests, documented tradeoffs, a working deployment — not a pile of unfinished scripts.

Complete means: commented contracts that flag their own teaching simplifications, tests that include fuzz and invariant checks beyond the happy path, a frontend that reads real on-chain state, a verified testnet deployment, and a README that explains your actual design decisions.
Next: choosing which project to emphasize, based on the kind of blockchain role you're actually aiming for.
